subject: Global cadence & availability handoff — proposed rotating demo windows
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmeanalytics.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@greenstack.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 15:10:00 -0400
Subject: Global cadence & availability handoff — proposed rotating demo windows

Thanks again for a productive discovery call this morning — appreciate the clarity on your main constraints (data residency, bursty inference for reports, and procurement timeline).

Quick recap and proposed next step: Laura (cc'd) would lead a 60–90min technical deep dive focused on integration points and performance expectations. To make this work for your US, EU, and APAC teams, we recommend trying a rotating weekly cadence (so the heavy technical slot moves through each region on a recurring schedule). That keeps the same meeting for all stakeholders but rotates local times to be fair.

Proposed rotation (start week of Aug 24):
- Slot A (US-friendly): Tue 09:00 ET / 14:00 BST / 15:00 CEST
- Slot B (EU-friendly): Wed 15:00 CEST / 10:00 ET / 23:00 SGT
- Slot C (APAC-friendly): Fri 08:00 SGT / Thu 19:00 CEST / Thu 14:00 ET

Please reply with: 1) your preferred slot(s) for the first two rotations, 2) any absolute blackout windows for engineers, and 3) whether a 60 or 90 minute deep dive is preferred. I attached an .ics with tentative slots and a short one-pager on what we'll cover.

Attachments: [acme-avails-rotating-slots.ics (text/calendar)], [redwood-demo-one-pager.pdf (application/pdf)]

Thanks — I’ll draft a rotating invite template once I have your preferences.

—
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmeanalytics.com>

Subject: Re: Global cadence & availability handoff — proposed rotating demo windows

Ben — thanks for the summary and for laying out the slots. This looks workable. A few quick notes from the Acme side: 

- We like the rotating approach to share load across teams.
- For the first two rotations, our preferred order is: Slot B (EU-friendly), Slot C (APAC-friendly). US team can take Slot A starting rotation 3.
- Blackouts: our infra lead (Jules) is unavailable Mon/Tue mornings CEST the next two weeks for release prep.
- Prefer 90 minutes for the deep dive so we can walk through realistic traces and have time for the engineers.

Looping in our procurement inbox (procurement@acmeanalytics.com) for timeline visibility — they may ask for a commercial summary before formal invites.

Appreciate it — will confirm exact attendee list after I check Jules' calendar.

—
Samantha Lee
Head of Platform Partnerships
Acme Analytics

Appreciate the quick reply, Samantha — that ordering works.

Plan based on your ask:
- Week 1 (Aug 24): Slot B (EU-friendly) — technical deep dive (90m) led by Laura
- Week 2 (Aug 31): Slot C (APAC-friendly) — 90m
- Week 3 (Sep 7): Slot A (US-friendly) — 90m

Operational notes:
- Laura, can you confirm a 90m agenda (pre-reads + time for a live perf run)?
- Evelyn, I’ve cc'd you to keep procurement/contract readiness in the loop — procurement asked for a one-page commercial summary & proposed SOW cadence, which I attached to this thread.

I’ll send provisional calendar invites marked "rotating — please accept only the instances your team can attend" and include a rotating-note in the invite description. If procurement wants a separate pre-meeting, we can schedule a short sync the week prior.

Quoted for context below.

—
Ben

Thanks — plan sounds good. A few technical constraints / asks from my side: 

1) Please share a short pre-read on data residency and retention so I can zero in on integration boundaries (Samantha — I saw you attached something; can you confirm it’s the latest?). If not, I’ve attached a short redwood doc for the call prep.
2) For the perf run we’ll need a sandbox token and a small sample of representative requests (preferably a JSONL with ~100 examples). If Acme can provide samples ahead of the deep dive, we can pre-warm caches and get better numbers.
3) I’ll block 90 minutes on the tentative calendar but may split into 60m + 30m follow-up if participants prefer that format.
